explanation: After the coup the military was more concerned with political control and left economic policy to a group of trusted technocrats under Delfim Netto, and the model that followed rested on low wages, rising exports and inflows of foreign capital — three things a government answerable to an electorate would have found harder to hold together. James Petras’s reading, which Wikipedia carries, makes the seizure of power and the system of military-police control part of what the growth was built on. `enabled`: the regime did not produce ten per cent a year by decree, but it is what made that particular model available.
